title: Episode 97: C++ vs Carbon vs Circle vs CppFront with Sean Baxter

sentences.en: I would like to encourage us, as a community of 7 million C++ developers around the world,
sentences.zh: 我想鼓励我们，作为全球 700 万 C++ 开发者的社区，

sentences.en: as we consider C++'s future, to push the boundaries to bring C++ itself forward and double down on C++, not be quick to switch to something else.
sentences.zh: 在我们思考 C++ 的未来时，要勇于突破界限，推动 C++ 自身向前发展，并坚定地支持 C++，而不是急于转向其他语言。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 97, recorded on September 25th, 2022.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 97 期，录制于 2022 年 9 月 25 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we talk to Sean Baxter about C++, carbon, circle, and CPP front.
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天我和联合主持人 Bryce 将与 Sean Baxter 一起聊聊 C++、Carbon、Circle 和 Cppfront。

sentences.en: We've got bidirectional is the infinity sign, omnidirectional is the circle,
sentences.zh: 我们有双向（bidirectional）即无穷大符号，全向（omnidirectional）即圆圈，

sentences.en: Dario is the overlapping Venn diagram, and cardio is the...
sentences.zh: Dario 是重叠的维恩图，而 cardio 是……

sentences.en: Okay, which one do I want to be on?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想选哪一个？

sentences.en: Probably omni, or yeah, omnidirectional.
sentences.zh: 大概是全向，或者，对，全向。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm sorry, Connor, Connor, there are four signals.
sentences.zh: 好吧，抱歉，Connor，Connor，有四个信号。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, right, the circle, the circle, the circle.
sentences.zh: 哦对，没错，圆圈，圆圈，圆圈。

sentences.en: It's topical that this is a perfect segue into having Sean Baxter.
sentences.zh: 这正好是一个完美的过渡，引出我们的嘉宾 Sean Baxter。

sentences.en: Better not be cons and rocks.
sentences.zh: 最好别是骗局（cons）和石头（rocks）。

sentences.en: Alright, so we should introduce our gueSt.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们该介绍我们的嘉宾了。

sentences.en: Yeah, Bryce, you can take this introduction.
sentences.zh: 好的，Bryce，你来做这个介绍吧。

sentences.en: Hang on, my dog is staring dead into my eyes right now.
sentences.zh: 等等，我的狗现在正死死地盯着我看。

sentences.en: Alright, I am here in my lovely Manhattan apartment with Sean Baxter, the creator of the Circle Compiler, which I personally think is the future of C++.
sentences.zh: 好了，我现在在曼哈顿可爱的公寓里，和 Sean Baxter 在一起，他是 Circle 编译器的创造者，我个人认为那是 C++ 的未来。

sentences.en: Sean, maybe you should introduce yourself.
sentences.zh: Sean，也许你应该自我介绍一下。

sentences.en: Thanks for the introduction, Bryce.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你的介绍，Bryce。

sentences.en: Hi, Connor.
sentences.zh: 你好，Connor。

sentences.en: I'm here to, I guess for a really aggressive interview, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 我来这里，我想是为了接受一场非常激烈的采访，听起来是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's correct.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: An adversarial one.
sentences.zh: 一场对抗性的采访。

sentences.en: I'll try to stay in my toes.
sentences.zh: 我会尽量保持警惕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Did you listen to the last episode?
sentences.zh: 你听了上一期节目吗？

sentences.en: Because what happened when, I'm not even sure I'm allowed to mention it, but we, Bryce, I was asking Bryce if we were going to talk about some topical news
sentences.zh: 因为当时发生了什么，我甚至不确定我是否被允许提及它，但是我们，Bryce，我当时在问 Bryce 我们是否要谈论一些热门新闻，

sentences.en: that had come out in the last previous week and then about a sort of successor to C++ kind of area and then he was like, oh, do you mean jacked?
sentences.zh: 那些在上周刚出来的，关于某种 C++ 后继者领域的新闻，然后他说，哦，你是说 Carbon 吗？

sentences.en: Or no, first you said, oh, do you mean Val?
sentences.zh: 或者不，你先说，哦，你是说 Val 吗？

sentences.en: And then I said, no, you know I don't mean Val.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，不，你知道我指的不是 Val。

sentences.en: And then he said, oh, you mean jacked?
sentences.zh: 然后他说，哦，你是说 Carbon 吗？

sentences.en: And then out of that, he said, oh, we should bring on Sean Baxter because Sean has looked at all of the languages that are supposedly going to replace C++
sentences.zh: 然后在那之后，他说，哦，我们应该请 Sean Baxter 来，因为 Sean 研究过所有那些据称要取代 C++ 的语言，

sentences.en: and has opinions to share, including obviously.
sentences.zh: 并且有观点要分享，显然包括这些。

sentences.en: I think more importantly, before everybody decided they wanted to make a successor language to C++, like predating it by like three or four years,
sentences.zh: 我觉得更重要的是，在每个人都决定要制造一种 C++ 后继语言之前，大概提前了三四年，

sentences.en: Sean decided he wanted to make C++ better.
sentences.zh: Sean 就决定他想让 C++ 变得更好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And for the, I mean, we should, yeah, do like, you should introduce yourself a bit for any of the people that haven't listened.
sentences.zh: 而且对于，我是说，我们应该，是的，做点什么，你应该为那些没听过节目的听众做个自我介绍。

sentences.en: You have, I think, two different interviews, one on CppCast and one on CppChat.
sentences.zh: 我想你有两次不同的采访，一次在 CppCast，一次在 CppChat。

sentences.en: And I distinctly recall being in Sunnyvale.
sentences.zh: 我清楚地记得当时在桑尼维尔。

sentences.en: And I think I was either on a bike ride or on a run when I was listening to that CppChat episode.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时要么在骑车，要么在跑步，听着那期 CppChat 节目。

sentences.en: And I like, I was like floored because they were just, you were just talking about how you had written a C++ compiler, like single-handedly by yourself.
sentences.zh: 我当时简直惊呆了，因为他们只是，你当时在谈论你是如何单枪匹马写出一个 C++ 编译器的。

sentences.en: And I was like, wait, what?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，等等，什么？

sentences.en: And you were, and then I think it was like, I can't remember.
sentences.zh: 然后你当时，我想大概是，我不记得了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was probably the CppChat one.
sentences.zh: 是的，可能就是 CppChat 那次。

sentences.en: And the hosts were just like, well, let me get this straight.
sentences.zh: 主持人当时就像是，好吧，让我理清一下。

sentences.en: Over three years, or I think it was two or three years, you just single-handedly by yourself.
sentences.zh: 在三年，或者我想是两三年里，你就单枪匹马一个人。

sentences.en: Like meanwhile, the other people implementing compilers or teams, scores of people, and you just did it single-handedly.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，其他人实现编译器都是团队作战，几十个人，而你只是单枪匹马做到了。

sentences.en: So anyways, you can.
sentences.zh: 所以不管怎样，你可以。

sentences.en: Right, so it's been six years now that I quit my job.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以我辞职到现在已经六年了。

sentences.en: I had this epiphany about compilers.
sentences.zh: 我当时对编译器有了一个顿悟。

sentences.en: And I thought, like the initial idea was to rotate the language from the compile time into the runtime domain.
sentences.zh: 我想，最初的想法是将语言从编译时领域旋转到运行时领域。

sentences.en: Or rather, let me say that again.
sentences.zh: 或者更确切地说，让我再说一遍。

sentences.en: To rotate the language from the runtime to the compile time domain.
sentences.zh: 将语言从运行时领域旋转到编译时领域。

sentences.en: So what used to be code that you could build and execute at runtime, you could evaluate it through the interpreter at compile time.
sentences.zh: 所以以前那些你可以在运行时构建和执行的代码，现在可以通过解释器在编译时进行求值。

sentences.en: And that way, all the standard library and pretty much all code would be available to you to use for compile time programming.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，所有的标准库和几乎所有的代码都可以供你进行编译时编程。

sentences.en: And that was the impetus.
sentences.zh: 这就是动力所在。

sentences.en: So I have a meta token that you can put in front of a statement.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一个元标记（meta token），你可以把它放在语句前面。

sentences.en: And it'll evaluate that and create that object at compile time.
sentences.zh: 它会对其进行求值并在编译时创建该对象。

sentences.en: And there's no like, it doesn't care about constexpr or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 而且它不像 constexpr 那样有那么多限制。

sentences.en: So you can have mutable state.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以拥有可变状态。

sentences.en: And it kind of blurs the line between a compile language and an interpretive language.
sentences.zh: 它模糊了编译语言和解释型语言之间的界限。

sentences.en: It's still statically typed.
sentences.zh: 它仍然是静态类型的。

sentences.en: It still generates object code at the end.
sentences.zh: 它最终仍然生成目标代码。

sentences.en: But now you have access to a greater vocabulary of functions and types to do your work.
sentences.zh: 但现在你可以使用更丰富的函数和类型词汇来完成工作。

sentences.en: So you can open a file at compile time, read in data, and then kind of reflect on that data to emit code programmatically.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在编译时打开一个文件，读取数据，然后对这些数据进行反射，从而以编程方式发出代码。

sentences.en: And that was, you know, that was the original idea.
sentences.zh: 这就是，你知道，最初的想法。

sentences.en: And it was actually a really great way to start running a compiler because I didn't have to worry about LLM at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 而且这实际上是开始运行编译器的一个非常好的方法，因为我一开始不必担心 LLVM。

sentences.en: I could just use the interpreter and evaluate my own source code at compile time.
sentences.zh: 我可以只使用解释器并在编译时评估我自己的源代码。

sentences.en: So that was an easier way to bring it up.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种更容易将其启动起来的方法。

sentences.en: So instead of having to worry about a front end and back end, building both of these simultaneously, it was like, I'll just build the front end.
sentences.zh: 所以不必担心前端和后端，不必同时构建这两者，就像是，我只构建前端。

sentences.en: I'll try to consume all of the, you know, STL headers.
sentences.zh: 我会尝试消费所有的，你知道，STL 头文件。

sentences.en: I'll try to consume, you know, other kind of open source projects to get this thing built.
sentences.zh: 我会尝试消费，你知道，其他类型的开源项目来构建这个东西。

sentences.en: And then instead of worrying about emitting object code, I could just run it inside the compiler.
sentences.zh: 然后不必担心发出目标代码，我可以直接在编译器内部运行它。

sentences.en: And that was a good way to bring it up.
sentences.zh: 这是一个启动它的好方法。

sentences.en: That's pretty, pretty amazing.
sentences.zh: 那真是太令人惊叹了。

sentences.en: So, but I want to, I want to, I want to, I want to go back to the first part of that amazing story, which is you quit your job.
sentences.zh: 所以，但我想要，我想要，我想要，我想要回到那个惊人故事的第一部分，也就是你辞职了。

sentences.en: You believe in this so much that like, just, just, just take me through that.
sentences.zh: 你对此如此坚信，以至于，就，就，带我了解一下那个过程。

sentences.en: Like you, you were had such conviction in this, that this needed to be built.
sentences.zh: 就像你，你对此有如此坚定的信念，认为这必须被创造出来。

sentences.en: Um, right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: I, I, I didn't really know what was in store for me and I'm not sure, I'm not sure I would do it again, but on the other hand, I think it's kind of in my nature to do this.
sentences.zh: 我，我真的不知道等待我的是什么，我也不确定，我不确定我是否会再做一次，但另一方面，我认为做这种事是我的天性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, it's been, I mean, it's been like really difficult.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这，我是说，这真的非常困难。

sentences.en: Um, and I haven't had any money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我没有任何钱。

sentences.en: I haven't had any income since then.
sentences.zh: 从那以后我就没有任何收入了。

sentences.en: So one motivating factor behind this is just like, I don't want to end up penniless and with nothing to show.
sentences.zh: 所以这背后的一个驱动因素就是，我不想最终身无分文，却一事无成。

sentences.en: So I put a lot of pressure on myself to produce, so I don't get bogged down in probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我给自己施加了很大的压力去产出，这样我就不会陷入问题中。

sentences.en: If I see a can of worms, I do not go open it.
sentences.zh: 如果我看到一个麻烦的源头，我就不会去打开它。

sentences.en: I try to, I try to stay productive and I just try to, to write code.
sentences.zh: 我尽量，我尽量保持高效，我只是尝试，去写代码。

sentences.en: And I have this sense of like, just being able to, to cruise through any issue.
sentences.zh: 而且我有一种感觉，就是能够，去克服任何问题。

sentences.en: And I think I've always had that kind of conviction.
sentences.zh: 我想我一直都有那种信念。

sentences.en: It's just a matter of willpower.
sentences.zh: 这只是意志力的问题。

sentences.en: So if I, if you have the idea and there's an idea that's attractive and if you consume enough willpower, then you should go and do it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有这个想法，而且这个想法很有吸引力，如果你消耗足够的意志力，那么你就应该去实现它。

sentences.en: I didn't have any other, you know, dependence or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我没有任何其他，你知道，依赖项之类的东西。

sentences.en: So might as well follow my dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 所以不如去追随我的梦想。

sentences.en: That makes things a little bit easier.
sentences.zh: 这让事情变得容易了一些。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I think since then circle has, um, evolved a lot and it's gone a lot of different directions.
sentences.zh: 但我认为从那以后 Circle 已经，嗯，进化了很多，并且走向了许多不同的方向。

sentences.en: So I have, um, I've had two distinct pattern matching implementations.
sentences.zh: 所以我已经，嗯，我有过两种不同的模式匹配实现。

sentences.en: I've had, um, a shader.
sentences.zh: 我有过，嗯，一个着色器。

sentences.en: I embedded the, uh, GLSL, OpenGL shader language into C++ and I can emit, uh, the spear B intermediate representation, which is used for, um, Vulcan and OpenGL code.
sentences.zh: 我将 GLSL，OpenGL 着色器语言嵌入到 C++ 中，我可以发出 SPIR-V 中间表示，它用于，嗯，Vulkan 和 OpenGL 代码。

sentences.en: So you can program, uh, any of the 12 shader stages in C++, just like you would CUDA.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以像使用 CUDA 一样，用 C++ 编写任何 12 个着色器阶段的程序。

sentences.en: I have like a CUDA to target.
sentences.zh: 我有一个类似 CUDA 的目标。

sentences.en: Um, and I've been, uh, CPP now, I, I gave a keynote on, uh, pack, uh, meta functions and enhanced parameter packs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我一直在，嗯，CPP Now，我，我做了一个关于，嗯，包，嗯，元函数和增强参数包的主题演讲。

sentences.en: It was a great talk.
sentences.zh: 那是一次很棒的演讲。

sentences.en: I loved the talk.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那次演讲。

sentences.en: I was, I was sad when people had so much constructive criticism afterwards, but I thought it was a great talk.
sentences.zh: 我当时，我当时很难过，因为后来人们提出了那么多建设性的批评，但我认为那是一次很棒的演讲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm just, I'm just trying to explore, um, different language ideas and some of these are really radical.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我只是，我只是在尝试探索，嗯，不同的语言想法，其中一些非常激进。

sentences.en: I don't think any of like these things I'm talking about aren't things that will appear in proposals.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我谈论的这些事情是那些会出现在提案中的东西。

sentences.en: And there's certainly one things that they're not things that are likely to be, um, standardized.
sentences.zh: 而且它们肯定不是那些可能被，嗯，标准化的东西。

sentences.en: But are they radical or are they radical for C++?
sentences.zh: 但它们是激进的，还是对 C++ 来说是激进的？

sentences.en: And like I asked that, like if C++ was a younger language or if C++ was evolved like some other languages are, would some of these proposals be seen as radical as they are in C++?
sentences.zh: 就像我问的那样，如果 C++ 是一门更年轻的语言，或者如果 C++ 像其他一些语言那样进化，那么其中一些提案会被视为像在 C++ 中那样激进吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Um, it's hard to say.
sentences.zh: 嗯，很难说。

sentences.en: I mean, we are where we are.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们现在就在这里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: So, uh, do you want to like pivot to the, uh, successor language question?
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，你想转到，嗯，后继语言的问题吗？

sentences.en: Because I think that is, I have a few, I have a few other, uh, uh, this is going to be awesome
sentences.zh: 因为我认为那是，我还有几个，我还有几个其他的，嗯，嗯，这会很棒，

sentences.en: because I'm just going to sit back and let Bryce, this, and so I'm just going to get like an advanced preview screening of this, uh, this, of this interview here.
sentences.zh: 因为我只是要坐下来，让 Bryce 来做，所以我就要得到一个关于这次采访的提前预览了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, so, so next, uh, uh, next discussion.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，所以下一个，嗯，嗯，下一个讨论。

sentences.en: Um, so circle is not open source.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以 Circle 不是开源的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people maybe find that surprising, um, in this day and age.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为很多人可能觉得这很令人惊讶，嗯，在当今时代。

sentences.en: Um, can you maybe explain why it's not open source?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你能解释一下为什么它不是开源的吗？

sentences.en: Um, yeah, I don't want to have to respond to people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我不想不得不去回应人们。

sentences.en: Um, I, I need to be able to sit back and think about things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我，我需要能够坐下来思考事情。

sentences.en: So for the last like three months, you know, two or three months, I've been thinking about generics and I have to be able to tune everything out.
sentences.zh: 所以过去大概三个月，你知道，两三个月，我一直在思考泛型，我必须能够屏蔽一切干扰。

sentences.en: And the idea about if you open source it and you have like pull requests and you have all these, uh, demands on your time.
sentences.zh: 关于如果你把它开源，然后你有类似拉取请求，你有所有这些，嗯，对你时间的索求的想法。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is still like a research language, even though it's a full compiler, it's 275,000 lines of, I've run a lot of test weeks through it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这仍然像是一门研究语言，尽管它是一个完整的编译器，它有 275,000 行代码，我运行了很多测试套件通过它。

sentences.en: For me, it's still about exploring ideas.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它仍然是关于探索想法。

sentences.en: And, you know, for me, I want to spend my time developing ideas.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，对我来说，我想把时间花在开发想法上。

sentences.en: And I think responding to, to users to like, and they have like, oh, there's so many, there's so many odd demands that I can't satisfy.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为回应，回应用户，就像，他们有类似，哦，有这么多，有这么多奇怪的要求我无法满足。

sentences.en: So I'm just trying to do the best I can.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是在尽我所能。

sentences.en: And at the same time, I feel like I don't owe anybody anything right now.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我觉得我现在不欠任何人任何东西。

sentences.en: It's not open source.
sentences.zh: 它不是开源的。

sentences.en: I'm not taking anyone's contributions.
sentences.zh: 我没有接受任何人的贡献。

sentences.en: Um, this is giving me more freedom to kind of build the tool and take it any, any, which way I want.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这给了我更多的自由去构建这个工具，并以我想要的任何方式去发展它。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，他们，他们正在投入大量的，呃，投资在，在，在这些接口，嗯，或者这些，这些，这些特征上。

sentences.en: Uh, the other thing is, uh, some types, they have a choice type, which is just like the rust enum and they have a first class, um, tuple.
sentences.zh: 呃，另一件事是，呃，和类型（sum types），他们有一个选择类型（choice type），这就像 Rust 的枚举，而且他们有一个一等，嗯，元组。

sentences.en: And, uh, so when, when carbon was announced, you know, I, I, I thought like, you know, what is, what is getting the developers excited about this?
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，所以当，当 Carbon 被宣布时，你知道，我，我，我想，你知道，什么，什么让开发者对这个感到兴奋？

sentences.en: And it seems to be this new set of features, but all of these things can be implemented in C++, especially something like, uh, like a, some type of, uh, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且似乎是这一套新特性，但所有这些东西都可以在 C++ 中实现，特别是像，呃，像某种，呃，你知道，

sentences.en: language level variant.
sentences.zh: 语言级的变体（variant）。

sentences.en: That's like, it's really easy.
sentences.zh: 那就像，这真的很容易。

sentences.en: It's just in their data type.
sentences.zh: 它只是在他们的数据类型中。

sentences.en: It's just a, you know, a tagged union with some compiler generated, uh, constructors and assignment operators.
sentences.zh: 它只是一个，你知道，一个带有编译器生成的，呃，构造函数和赋值运算符的标记联合（tagged union）。

sentences.en: So I implemented that, um, pretty early on after the carbon announcement, I implemented the question mark operator from rust, which is the propagation.
sentences.zh: 所以我实现了那个，嗯，在 Carbon 公告发布后很早就实现了，我实现了来自 Rust 的问号运算符，也就是传播。

sentences.en: So that if you have a, uh, uh, a choice type called result and has an okay field and an error field, um, you can use the, uh, comma operator.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一个，呃，呃，名为 result 的选择类型，并且有一个 ok 字段和一个 error 字段，嗯，你可以使用，呃，逗号运算符。

sentences.en: And at, uh, at runtime, it'll examine the, um, active element of the, uh, choice type and it'll return, it'll either yield the okay element or it'll return the error.
sentences.zh: 而且在，呃，在运行时，它会检查，嗯，选择类型的活动元素，它会返回，它要么产生 ok 元素，要么返回错误。

sentences.en: Um, and this is a way to like propagate errors without exceptions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一种像在没有异常的情况下传播错误的方法。

sentences.en: And this is what you need, um, with, when you're like using these factory functions, since you don't have constructors, uh, a factory function would return a result of the,
sentences.zh: 而且这是你需要的，嗯，当你像使用这些工厂函数时，因为你没有构造函数，呃，工厂函数会返回一个结果，那个类型逗号，无论错误代码是什么。

sentences.en: that type comma, whatever the error code is.
sentences.zh: 然后你将能够使用逗号运算符来链接传播，而且，嗯，不需要大量的输入，拥有一种，一种静态异常处理。

sentences.en: And then you would be able to use the comma operator to chain the propagation and, um, without a whole bunch of typing, have a, a kind of static exception handling.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有用于，呃，一等语言元组的语法。

sentences.en: Um, there's syntax for, uh, first class language tuples.
sentences.zh: 所以它就像逗号分隔的类型列表或逗号分隔的，呃，表达式列表。

sentences.en: So it's just like comma separated list of types or comma separated list of, uh, expressions.
sentences.zh: 最后是概念，或者，什么，呃，Carbon 称之为接口。

sentences.en: And then finally there's concepts or what, what, uh, carbon is calling interfaces.
sentences.zh: 为了不把它们与 C++ 概念混淆。

sentences.en: So as not to confuse them with C++ concepts.
sentences.zh: 所以我回到了 2007、2008 年的档案，我翻出了旧的 C++ OX，呃，概念措辞。

sentences.en: So I went back to the archives to like 2007, 2008, and I dug up the old C++ OX, uh, concept wording.
sentences.zh: 那是一百页的措辞，Doug Greger，主要是 Doug Greger。

sentences.en: It's like a hundred pages of wording, Doug Greger, mostly Doug Greger.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且有像，有印第安纳学派，还有，嗯，德克萨斯大学，我想。

sentences.en: Um, and there was like, there's the Indiana school and there's the, um, Texas university of Texas, I guess.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 而且有某种，经过几年的来回，他们有了一个，嗯，呃，某种关于这个的联合提案。

sentences.en: And there was kind of a, after a few years of back and forth, they had a, um, uh, kind of a joint proposal for this.
sentences.zh: 而且它被合并到了语言中。

sentences.en: And it was merged into the language.
sentences.zh: 然后我认为在 2009 年，它全部被移除了。

sentences.en: And then I think in 2009, it was all removed.
sentences.zh: 然后我们一直没有异常直到 C++ 20。

sentences.en: And then we went without exceptions until C++ 20.
sentences.zh: 然后他们没有概念，或者说。

sentences.en: And then they were without concepts rather.
sentences.zh: 然后我们得到的概念是轻量级概念，基本上只是，呃，围绕 enable_if 的装饰。

sentences.en: And then concepts we got were concepts light, which are basically just, uh, porcelain around, porcelain around enable if.
sentences.zh: 所以它，它真的算是阉割了这个特性，但那个概念，嗯，来自，你知道，2006 年的特性。

sentences.en: So it's, it's really kind of gutted the feature, but that concept, um, feature from, you know, 2006.
sentences.zh: 正是 Carbon 真正押注其整个，嗯，核心的东西，也就是我们如何做重载以及我们如何做泛型？

sentences.en: Is exactly what carbon is staking really its entire, um, core on, which is how do we do, how do we do overloading and how do we do generics?
sentences.zh: 而且对他们来说，他们，他们说，我们想要拥有这些 C++ OX 概念。

sentences.en: And for them, they, they said, we want to have these C++ OX concepts.
sentences.zh: 他们使用术语接口，嗯，以使其与 C++ 现在中的概念区分开来。

sentences.en: They use the term interface, um, to keep it distinct from what concepts are in C++ now.
sentences.zh: 他们使用术语接口，嗯，以使其与 C++ 现在中的概念区分开来。

sentences.en: So I've been implementing that and it's been like really difficult, uh, but I, I think collectively I, I have,
sentences.zh: 我一直在实现这些功能，过程确实非常艰难，但我认为总的来说，我……

sentences.en: I have more confidence that these are the features that users want to see, because these are the users that, these are the features that persuaded Google management to be able to,
sentences.zh: 我更有信心认为这些正是用户想要的功能，因为这些功能说服了谷歌管理层，让他们能够……

sentences.en: you know, say, we want to fund this experiment and see where this experiment goes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，说我们愿意资助这个实验，看看这个实验最终会走向何方。

sentences.en: And you talk to a lot of other kind of C++ old timers and they, they are like really like Dave Abraham's at CPP now.
sentences.zh: 你和许多其他 C++ 老前辈交流时，他们现在真的很像 CPP 的 Dave Abrahams。

sentences.en: He was still agitated and angry about the removal of concepts back in 2009.
sentences.zh: 他当时对 2009 年移除 Concepts（概念）一事仍然感到愤慨和愤怒。

sentences.en: Like there was, there was like this led to a large schism in the C++, uh, leadership.
sentences.zh: 这导致了 C++ 领导层内部出现了巨大的分裂。

sentences.en: Um, arguably, I think if, if not for that schism, you know, it's possible that, uh, you know, the folks like Doug Greger and Dave Abrams,
sentences.zh: 可以说，如果不是因为那次分裂，你知道，很有可能像 Doug Gregor 和 Dave Abrahams 这样的人……

sentences.en: who went off to create Swift would have still been working on C++.
sentences.zh: 那些后来去创建 Swift 的人，可能还会继续致力于 C++。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think, I think this was a, a major defeat as far as like losing, um, you know, senior leadership.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一次重大失败，因为我们失去了高级领导层。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: And I, I think for some of the stuff we have to like, I think the committee process has been not optimal for C++ because people really, people really go to the mat.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为对于某些事情，我们必须……我认为委员会的流程对 C++ 来说并不理想，因为人们真的会据理力争。

sentences.en: The beginning of the episode, the cold open.
sentences.zh: 这一集的开头，冷开场。

sentences.en: I think a lot of the, um, the voters, they go to the mat about what, if they like a feature or not, they think it's a good feature.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多投票者，他们会为了自己是否喜欢某个功能，或者是否认为它是一个好功能而据理力争。

sentences.en: And, and that's important, but that's not the only concern.
sentences.zh: 这很重要，但这并不是唯一的考量。

sentences.en: I think keeping the community together is, is another concern.
sentences.zh: 我认为保持社区的团结是另一个考量。

sentences.en: And that's something I've learned writing a compiler.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在编写编译器过程中学到的。

sentences.en: A lot of the features I implement are not things I care about particularly.
sentences.zh: 我实现的很多功能并不是我特别关心的。

sentences.en: Like these generics I'm putting in, I don't really care about, about C++ OX concepts or Rust traits.
sentences.zh: 比如我正在加入的这些泛型，我其实并不关心 C++0x 的 Concepts 或者 Rust 的 Traits。

sentences.en: Um, but I know that a lot of other people really care about them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我知道很多人真的很关心它们。

sentences.en: I mean, they really care about them.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们真的很在乎。

sentences.en: And, and, you know, I'll, I'll believe them in that and I'll put the effort in to, to make that happen.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我会相信他们，并投入精力去实现这些功能。

sentences.en: And I think it's kind of important that we give other people who've over time proven themselves to be thoughtful, capable people.
sentences.zh: 我认为很重要的一点是，我们要给予那些随着时间推移证明了自己深思熟虑、能力出众的人以信任。

sentences.en: We need to give them the benefit of the doubt and say, if they're really interested in these features, we should put that in the language.
sentences.zh: 我们需要给予他们信任，如果他们真的对这些功能感兴趣，我们就应该把它们加入到语言中。

sentences.en: Even if I'm not personally into it, because otherwise it prevents the language from moving forward.
sentences.zh: 即使我个人并不感兴趣，因为否则的话，这会阻碍语言的发展。

sentences.en: We're never going to get a hundred percent agreement on really anything.
sentences.zh: 我们永远不可能在任何事情上达成百分之百的共识。

sentences.en: So I think we need to kind of like give ourselves, um, you know, more of a benefit of the doubt when it comes to adopting features.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在采用新功能时，我们需要给予彼此更多的信任。

sentences.en: The language won't, won't evolve otherwise.
sentences.zh: 否则这门语言就不会进化。

sentences.en: In doing your historical deep dive, was it documented why they ended up, um, getting rid of them?
sentences.zh: 在你进行历史回顾时，是否有文档记录他们最终为什么要废除这些功能？

sentences.en: Like, obviously there was folks on the committee that obviously weren't a fan of it.
sentences.zh: 显然委员会里有人并不喜欢它。

sentences.en: Like it was there, what was the justification?
sentences.zh: 当时到底有什么正当理由？

sentences.en: Oh, but buddy, you're, you're going to have to, uh, that's a whole nother episode where we get, we get some people from that time period on to talk about.
sentences.zh: 噢，老兄，你得……那是另一集的内容了，我们得请那个时期的人来谈谈。

sentences.en: Well, no, I mean, I've, I was curious too, just from a technical standpoint, because like the wording they have isn't, I mean, it's, it's okay.
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，我也很好奇，纯粹从技术角度来看，因为他们留下的措辞……我是说，还行吧。

sentences.en: It's doesn't answer all my questions and there's really nobody to go and ask anymore because we're stuck.
sentences.zh: 它并没有回答我所有的问题，而且现在已经没人可以去问了，因为我们卡住了。

sentences.en: We're talking about like language that's 15 years old.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论的是一门 15 年前的语言。

sentences.en: Um, I think there was an issue, a disagreement between like Bjarn's camp, Bjarn's camp that wanted a implicit concept map.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为当时 Bjarn 的阵营和另一方之间存在分歧，Bjarn 的阵营想要隐式概念映射（implicit concept map）。

sentences.en: So that, uh, if a type is probed and this type is determined to satisfy the requirements of the interface, then it satisfies the interface as opposed to explicit concept map.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，如果一个类型被探测到满足接口要求，那么它就满足该接口，而不是显式概念映射。

sentences.en: Um, it's just like a choice of defaults.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就像是默认值的选择问题。

sentences.en: And I think there were a lot of those.
sentences.zh: 我想当时有很多这样的情况。

sentences.en: And then the time was running out to get something into 11.
sentences.zh: 而且当时要把东西塞进 C++11 的时间已经不多了。

sentences.en: And at the end, instead of like getting consensus on what the default should be, um, the rest of the C++ committee members just decided to remove the feature.
sentences.zh: 最后，他们没有就默认值达成共识，而是决定直接移除该功能。

sentences.en: These are like, well, the clock's running down.
sentences.zh: 就像是，好吧，时间不多了。

sentences.en: We don't want to ship something that we don't have consensus on.
sentences.zh: 我们不想发布一个没有达成共识的功能。

sentences.en: So they removed the feature and then they never really got back to work on it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们移除了这个功能，之后就再也没有真正去处理它了。

sentences.en: At that point, they just moved on.
sentences.zh: 在那一点上，他们就直接放弃了。

sentences.en: Um, I mean, I'm sure there's like a lot of, uh, interpersonal conflicts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我肯定当时有很多个人冲突。

sentences.en: No, I think there, I think there were, but, um, it was a combination of a variety of technical disagreements.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为确实有，但这是多种技术分歧的综合结果。

sentences.en: And then those led to a variety of interpersonal arguments.
sentences.zh: 然后这些分歧导致了各种人际争论。

sentences.en: And, um, uh, I, I think it reached a point where both camps became very entrenched.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为双方都变得非常固执。

sentences.en: And, um, there wasn't really a, uh, uh, a compromise to be found.
sentences.zh: 嗯，真的找不到什么折中方案。

sentences.en: Um, I, I, I tend to not particularly like the design of the concepts that we got.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我个人不太喜欢我们最终得到的 Concepts 设计。

sentences.en: Um, I think that the, uh, the OX concepts design was much more natural and much more how I would imagine.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为 C++0x 的 Concepts 设计要自然得多，也更符合我的想象。

sentences.en: Like when I, when I, when I write up in like comments, like what a concept should look like, it's much, um,
sentences.zh: 比如当我写注释描述一个 Concept 应该是什么样子时，它更……

sentences.en: uh, you know, like I, I define sort of like the, you know, uh, uh, the, the archetype of, of what it would look like.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我定义了它看起来应该是什么样子的原型。

sentences.en: And that's much more what the C++ OX concepts look like.
sentences.zh: 那更接近 C++0x Concepts 的样子。

sentences.en: Whereas with, um, with the concepts that we have, you have to like write out these like examples of like how it'll be used.
sentences.zh: 而我们现在的 Concepts，你必须写出这些使用示例。

sentences.en: And I just find that supremely weird.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这极其奇怪。

sentences.en: Well, the concepts we have now, uh, don't do type checking at definition.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们现在的 Concepts 在定义时不做类型检查。

sentences.en: That's the big difference.
sentences.zh: 这就是最大的区别。

sentences.en: Like, um, rust traits and what they're trying to put into carbon, which they're calling interface.
sentences.zh: 比如 Rust 的 Traits，以及他们试图放入 Carbon 中的东西，他们称之为接口（interface）。

sentences.en: Um, and, and the Swift protocols, which is actually separate compilation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有 Swift 的协议（protocols），那实际上是单独编译的。

sentences.en: Uh, and, and there's like a runtime penalty for using the generics and Swift, but, but, but the general form is the same.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在 Swift 中使用泛型会有运行时开销，但总体形式是一样的。

sentences.en: Again, that's, that type checking is done, uh, at definition.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，那种类型检查是在定义时完成的。

sentences.en: So you write your, um, function generic and, uh, each of the, uh, template parameters, the generic parameters subscribes to some number of interfaces.
sentences.zh: 所以你编写泛型函数，每个模板参数、泛型参数都遵循一定数量的接口。

sentences.en: So it says like, this is an input iterator and that input iterator has a bunch of refinements indicating, you know, it's regular, it can be copied this way.
sentences.zh: 它会说，这是一个输入迭代器，该迭代器有一系列细化，表明它是常规的，可以这样复制。

sentences.en: And it has these operations.
sentences.zh: 它有这些操作。

sentences.en: And only those operations, uh, that are parts of the interfaces for each of the, for each of the data types can be used inside that function.
sentences.zh: 只有那些作为每个数据类型接口一部分的操作，才能在该函数内部使用。

sentences.en: If you use any other thing, then you get a, an error at definition.
sentences.zh: 如果你使用了其他任何东西，那么在定义时就会报错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Uh, in C++ 20 concepts, the concepts are just, uh, an enable if check.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在 C++20 的 Concepts 中，它们只是一个 enable_if 检查。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So if you get past that function declaration into the body, the concepts at that point are moot.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你通过了函数声明进入函数体，那么 Concepts 在那时就毫无意义了。

sentences.en: They're not operative anymore.
sentences.zh: 它们不再起作用了。

sentences.en: And, and I think the question of whether we could do type checking with OX concepts, that was really sort of what killed it was that they believed that, um,
sentences.zh: 我认为关于我们是否能用 C++0x 的 Concepts 进行类型检查的问题，这才是真正扼杀它的原因，因为他们认为……

sentences.en: that it would become impractical or, uh, computationally impractical or something to that effect.
sentences.zh: 这在计算上会变得不切实际，或者类似的情况。

sentences.en: Um, or the, or it would be too complex.
sentences.zh: 嗯，或者说它会太复杂。

sentences.en: Um, but then we ended up with this concepts light and without, and you should, you certainly can't do type checking in that model.
sentences.zh: 但最终我们得到了这种“轻量级 Concepts”，在这种模型下你肯定无法进行类型检查。

sentences.en: Um, but without that, what's really the value of concepts?
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果没有那个，Concepts 的价值到底在哪里？

sentences.en: Like it, it doesn't really seem to me like it delivers anything more than a smarter enable if.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它似乎并没有带来比更智能的 enable_if 更多的东西。

sentences.en: It was promised that it was going to give us these better diagnostics.
sentences.zh: 当初承诺它会给我们带来更好的诊断信息。

sentences.en: And I will admit the past like year, the diagnostics have gotten slightly better, but it really does not, I think, substantially enhance the, uh,
sentences.zh: 我承认过去一年里，诊断信息确实稍微好了一些，但我认为它并没有实质性地增强……

sentences.en: the diagnostic experience in the ways that we thought it would.
sentences.zh: 我们预想中的那种诊断体验。

sentences.en: Um, and it, yeah, like I don't really see what the tangible benefits are other than it's a cleaner way to do enable if.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，除了作为一种更简洁的 enable_if 实现方式外，我真的没看到什么实质性的好处。

sentences.en: I don't think we have to worry about C++ 20 concepts because we have evidence coming from these successor languages.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们需要担心 C++20 的 Concepts，因为我们有来自这些后续语言的证据。

sentences.en: Swift has the protocols, Rust has the traits, uh, and, you know, now there's like a decade of, uh, usage experience where the customers are more or less satisfied with that,
sentences.zh: Swift 有协议，Rust 有 Traits，而且现在已经有十年的使用经验了，用户对那种函数与调用者之间的契约或多或少是满意的。

sentences.en: with that, um, kind of contract between the, the function and the caller.
sentences.zh: 那种契约。

sentences.en: And I think it makes sense now that we have, you know, so much usage knowledge to try to, to go back and, and implement that in C++.
sentences.zh: 我认为既然我们现在有了这么多的使用经验，回过头来在 C++ 中实现它是有意义的。

sentences.en: So, so what I've been doing is like, I, I have, um, archetype establishment, which is when you mark up your function template with all these interfaces,
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在做的是，我有原型建立（archetype establishment），也就是当你用所有这些接口标记函数模板时……

sentences.en: it's the conjunction of these interfaces, um, indicating the, the, um, capabilities of the types.
sentences.zh: 这是这些接口的结合，表明了类型的能力。

sentences.en: Like, like that is hard to use internally.
sentences.zh: 这在内部很难使用。

sentences.en: And I think the problem is that if you were to specialize a class template over one of these archetypes, um, in the current C++ scheme,
sentences.zh: 我认为问题在于，如果你要在当前的 C++ 方案中针对这些原型之一特化类模板……

sentences.en: you can't use any of those member functions because those member functions are only known once that, um, that class template is specialized with real types.
sentences.zh: 你无法使用任何成员函数，因为只有当类模板用真实类型特化时，这些成员函数才可知。

sentences.en: Which is during instantiation, because you don't know if it's going to hit a partial template specialization, if it's going to hit an explicit, like explicit specialization.
sentences.zh: 也就是在实例化期间，因为你不知道它会命中部分模板特化，还是显式特化。

sentences.en: So I've been going through and like creating new kinds of fundamental data types.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在尝试创建新型的基础数据类型。

sentences.en: So I have, uh, class generics and choice generics.
sentences.zh: 所以我有了类泛型（class generics）和选择泛型（choice generics）。

sentences.en: So if you have, um, you know, template with the template parameter list class foo, that's a current, that's the regular class template.
sentences.zh: 如果你有模板参数列表 class foo，那是当前的常规类模板。

sentences.en: But if you have generic with the template argument list class foo, now foo is a, uh, is a class generic and that will actually,
sentences.zh: 但如果你有模板参数列表 class foo 的泛型，现在 foo 就是一个类泛型，它实际上……

sentences.en: that has a guarantee that there's no partial or explicit specializations.
sentences.zh: 它保证没有部分特化或显式特化。

sentences.en: And it allows you to, um, to see the, uh, the, the members of that class at definition.
sentences.zh: 它允许你在定义时看到该类的成员。

sentences.en: So I think the problem is that, and maybe this was a problem back 15 years ago was that C++ didn't really have the full vocabulary to support, um,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为问题在于，也许 15 年前的问题就是 C++ 没有完整的词汇表来支持……

sentences.en: early type checking in a way that was like convenient.
sentences.zh: 以一种方便的方式进行早期类型检查。

sentences.en: But, but I think a lot of the decisions for generics and Rust and Swift, and I'm sure Carbon, when it kind of shakes out, is going to, um,
sentences.zh: 但我认为 Rust 和 Swift 中泛型的许多决策，我相信 Carbon 在成熟后也会……

sentences.en: to limit partial specialization and explicit specialization to allow you to fully type check the data members of a, of a class that you're using inside a generic function.
sentences.zh: 限制部分特化和显式特化，以允许你对泛型函数内部使用的类的数据成员进行完全的类型检查。

sentences.en: So I've got,
sentences.zh: 所以我已经……

sentences.en: I've just got like a whole bunch of things in flight now to try to bring the new features that are promised by Carbon into C++ without having any like concern about breaking compatibility.
sentences.zh: 我手头有一大堆事情在进行，试图将 Carbon 承诺的新功能引入 C++，同时不用担心破坏兼容性。

sentences.en: Because it's written, it's all embedded in, in, you know, existing C++ compiler.
sentences.zh: 因为它是写在现有的 C++ 编译器中的。

sentences.en: And what's your motivation for doing that?
sentences.zh: 你这样做的动机是什么？

sentences.en: My, my motivation?
sentences.zh: 我的动机？

sentences.en: Well, I, I'm always looking for features that are going to...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我一直在寻找那些能够……的功能。

sentences.en: That are going to bring you users, yeah.
sentences.zh: 能够为你带来用户的那些功能，是吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, it can be the hit feature.
sentences.zh: 是的，那可能是杀手级功能。

sentences.en: And I think that...
sentences.zh: 我认为……

sentences.en: But is your, is your point also that we don't need a successor language because we can make C++ better?
sentences.zh: 但你的观点是否也认为我们不需要后续语言，因为我们可以让 C++ 变得更好？

sentences.en: Um, I don't think that's my, I mean, that might shake out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不认为那是我的……我是说，结果可能会是那样。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But it kind of is up to the people who help us successor languages.
sentences.zh: 但这取决于那些帮助开发后续语言的人。

sentences.en: Because if, if these successor languages work really well, then they can speak for themselves.
sentences.zh: 因为如果这些后续语言运行得非常好，那么它们自然会证明自己。

sentences.en: I'm, I'm just speaking for my evolution to C++.
sentences.zh: 我只是在为我的 C++ 进化论代言。

sentences.en: And I think that, um, you know, C++ gets a lot of flack, but I think we can still evolve it in any direction we want.
sentences.zh: 我认为 C++ 虽然受到很多批评，但我认为我们仍然可以随心所欲地进化它。

sentences.en: If we wanted to put VAL style value semantics in it, I think we could do that.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想在其中加入 VAL 风格的值语义，我认为我们可以做到。

sentences.en: I think we could evolve it in really almost any direction and, and still retain core, uh, compatibility with all the code out there.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以几乎向任何方向进化它，同时保留与现有所有代码的核心兼容性。

sentences.en: Yeah, I, I, I tend to agree with you.
sentences.zh: 是的，我倾向于同意你的观点。

sentences.en: Um, I think most of the C++ committee and most other implementers don't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为大多数 C++ 委员会成员和其他实现者并不这么想。

sentences.en: What, what, why do you think, why do you think so people, so few people see the potential for evolving C++?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么很少有人看到 C++ 进化的潜力？

sentences.en: Well, they don't want to have to do 20 years of, uh, proposal revisions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们不想经历 20 年的提案修订过程。

sentences.en: I mean, for some of these features there, they would take forever to get through the committee.
sentences.zh: 我是说，其中一些功能在委员会中通过需要永远的时间。

sentences.en: And I think, I mean.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为……

sentences.en: Right, and, and it's easier for, for one person or a small.
sentences.zh: 没错，而且对于一个人或一个小团队来说更容易。

sentences.en: Well, no, it just, the Google people who were already the major claim maintainers could have just forked claim and they could have built the carbon features straight into claim.
sentences.zh: 不，只是那些已经是 Clang 主要维护者的谷歌员工，他们本可以分叉 Clang，直接把 Carbon 的功能构建到 Clang 中。

sentences.en: And they could call it a successor language, that's fine, but it would have been a superset of C++.
sentences.zh: 他们可以称之为后续语言，那没问题，但它将是 C++ 的超集。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They could have had a new syntax.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以采用新的语法。

sentences.en: They could have, even if they wanted, made a context-free, a new context-free grammar that has not even all the features, but still plugs into the existing compiler.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至可以制作一种上下文无关的新语法，不需要包含所有功能，但仍然可以插入到现有的编译器中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Um, now I think that's just a different workflow, but it's one where at all points you can keep compiling a C++ hello world and you know it's going to work all the way through.
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在我认为那只是不同的工作流程，但在任何时候你都可以继续编译 C++ 的 Hello World，并且你知道它会一直有效。

sentences.en: And you can make your incremental changes and you can evolve it in any direction.
sentences.zh: 你可以进行增量更改，并向任何方向进化它。

sentences.en: And I think, um, you know, that's, that's what I'm doing and, and having a really nimble C++ compiler source base, you know, allows me to do that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是我正在做的事情，拥有一个非常灵活的 C++ 编译器源代码库，让我能够做到这一点。

sentences.en: And I think that's really the value.
sentences.zh: 我认为这才是真正的价值所在。

sentences.en: But you also, you don't have a committee of 300 people that you have to get to sign off on.
sentences.zh: 但你也不需要一个 300 人的委员会来签字批准。

sentences.en: But the claim, the claim maintainers don't have to do that either.
sentences.zh: 但 Clang 的维护者也不需要那样做。

sentences.en: They could have just said, we're going to fork carbon and carbon is going to be basically a claim with other features.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以说，我们要分叉 Carbon，Carbon 基本上就是一个带有其他功能的 Clang。

sentences.en: They didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 他们没有那样做。

sentences.en: Why don't they?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们不这样做？

sentences.en: Well, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, they, they have a different, different strategy and a different, I mean, they think differently of C++ than I think of it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们有不同的策略，而且他们对 C++ 的看法和我不同。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because I think they would argue that's not C++, that's C++ with extensions.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为他们会争辩说那不是 C++，那是带有扩展的 C++。

sentences.en: Well, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: What's the difference though?
sentences.zh: 不过区别到底在哪儿呢？

sentences.en: At what point does, does the circle dialect of C++ become its own language?
sentences.zh: C++ 的 Circle 方言在什么时候会演变成一门独立的语言？

sentences.en: This is, I don't think this is a, this is just a vocabulary distinction.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这只是词汇上的区别，并不算什么。

sentences.en: I don't think it has any, um, it doesn't affect anything.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它有什么……嗯，它不会影响任何东西。

sentences.en: If you're, what matters is if you're a company and you've got billions of dollars of value in C++ source spaces, um, you want to keep compiling that.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一家拥有数十亿美元 C++ 源代码资产的公司，你最看重的是能够持续编译这些代码。

sentences.en: You want to make sure that every year you get the new version out of your, of your, the new build out.
sentences.zh: 你想要确保每年都能发布新版本，都能构建出新的版本。

sentences.en: And it'd be great if the compiler improves with your own software.
sentences.zh: 如果编译器能随着你的软件一起改进，那就太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, and, and we can do that.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们完全可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Like we can, we can evolve C++ much more quickly and, and actually give users the features they want, uh, without having to break anything, you know, or if you do break,
sentences.zh: 我们可以更快速地演进 C++，真正为用户提供他们想要的功能，而无需破坏任何东西；或者即使有破坏，

sentences.en: it could be a tiny, like a small break.
sentences.zh: 那也可能只是非常微小的破坏。

sentences.en: I have, I've, I've gotten a lot more bold about my extensions recently.
sentences.zh: 最近，我在扩展功能方面变得大胆多了。

sentences.en: I've, I've realized I have, I have this pragma, like pound pragma feature and feature name.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我可以使用这种 pragma，比如 #pragma feature 和功能名称。

sentences.en: So I have one like pound pragma feature generics, pound pragma feature tuple, um, a couple others.
sentences.zh: 所以我有了像 #pragma feature generics、#pragma feature tuple 这样的功能，还有其他几个。

sentences.en: And, and what they do is they draw new tokens, but only for the file.
sentences.zh: 它们的作用是引入新的标记（tokens），但仅限于该文件内。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I can pound pragma feature generics and then include any STL header.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以加上 #pragma feature generics，然后包含任何 STL 头文件。

sentences.en: And I know it won't conflict with this new tokens I brought in because the token scope is only in that file and I can turn it off if I want.
sentences.zh: 我知道它不会与我引入的新标记冲突，因为标记的作用域仅在该文件中，而且如果我想的话，还可以随时关闭它。

sentences.en: So, and now I realize, well, why not just like, you know, evolve really rapidly.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在意识到，为什么不直接快速演进呢？

sentences.en: I'm not, I know I'm not going to break anything because the syntax is gating, um, or that, that, that pragma is, is gating which source, uh, lines are exposed to the new features.
sentences.zh: 我知道我不会破坏任何东西，因为语法是受控的，或者说那个 pragma 控制了哪些源代码行可以使用这些新功能。

sentences.en: And, you know, you just, just try it out.
sentences.zh: 而且，你只需要试一试就行了。

sentences.en: I keep turning it over and over.
sentences.zh: 我一直在反复思考这个问题。

sentences.en: And so I've been turning over, uh, these function generics, the class generics, tuples, choice types.
sentences.zh: 我一直在琢磨函数泛型、类泛型、元组、选择类型这些东西。

sentences.en: And I'm, I'm just trying to go through the checklist because I think on every metric, an extended C++ can be competitive with the new features that Carbon wants to offer.
sentences.zh: 我只是想完成这份清单，因为我认为从各项指标来看，扩展后的 C++ 完全可以与 Carbon 想要提供的新功能相媲美。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Without any question about, well, it's not going to support exceptions.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，它不会不支持异常。

sentences.en: It's not going to support, you know, function overloading.
sentences.zh: 它也不会不支持函数重载。

sentences.en: Uh, yeah, for me, this is, this is the way to move forward.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对我来说，这就是前进的方向。

sentences.en: And I'm, I'm very,
sentences.zh: 而且我非常……

sentences.en: I'm actually happy with the successor language of big languages because it's me and there's other people thinking about what features are important and then I can go and, you know,
sentences.zh: 我其实对大型语言的继任者感到满意，因为不仅是我，还有其他人也在思考哪些功能是重要的，然后我就可以去，你知道的，

sentences.en: implement those in my own system.
sentences.zh: 在我的系统中实现这些功能。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I, I do agree with you.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实同意你的观点。

sentences.en: So I do suspect that in practice in the field, some of that, some of the ways in which we would evolve will become constrained by actual real world impacts of, um,
sentences.zh: 我怀疑在实际应用中，我们演进的一些方式会受到现实世界中产生破坏性变更所带来的影响的限制。

sentences.en: of making breaking changes.
sentences.zh: 做出破坏性变更的影响。

sentences.en: Um, but I, I, I think that, that the C++ evolution process is essentially become, uh, paralyzed by this, this, this fear of what will happen if we, uh, uh, make a breaking change.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，C++ 的演进过程本质上已经因为这种对“如果做出破坏性变更会发生什么”的恐惧而陷入了瘫痪。

sentences.en: And why is everyone talking, why, why is everyone so fixated on breaking changes?
sentences.zh: 为什么每个人都在谈论，为什么每个人都如此执着于破坏性变更？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: I mean, none of this has to like interface generics, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都不需要像接口泛型那样，对吧？

sentences.en: We can, we can, we can put these in and that doesn't break any code.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把这些加进去，而不会破坏任何代码。

sentences.en: Um, some types don't break any, people want pattern.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有些类型不会破坏任何东西，人们想要模式匹配。

sentences.en: It doesn't introduce new keywords.
sentences.zh: 它没有引入新的关键字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what I've, I, like I, like I said, I'm gating those pound pragma feature interface to your source file, your new source file, put that in, right?
sentences.zh: 所以就像我说的，我用 #pragma feature interface 把这些功能限制在你的源文件中，你的新源文件，放进去就行了，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't have to, you don't have to worry about all your system dependencies.
sentences.zh: 你不需要担心所有的系统依赖项。

sentences.en: And this has been a successful approach in other languages, right?
sentences.zh: 这种方法在其他语言中已经很成功了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Doesn't JavaScript do this?
sentences.zh: JavaScript 不就是这么做的吗？

sentences.en: Don't they have, uh, uh, you're, you're the programming language person, Connor.
sentences.zh: 他们没有吗……你是编程语言专家，Connor。

sentences.en: I expect you to know this.
sentences.zh: 我指望你知道这个。

sentences.en: I don't know anything about JavaScript other than they got like 17 different ways to compare things.
sentences.zh: 除了知道 JavaScript 有 17 种比较东西的方法外，我对它一无所知。

sentences.en: And so what everyone whines about is triple equals, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 大家都在抱怨什么三重等于号之类的。

sentences.en: Um, no, I believe JavaScript has a new strict thing that if you do it, it gives you more modern.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，我相信 JavaScript 有一种新的严格模式，如果你使用它，就能获得更现代的特性。

sentences.en: Well, I, I just think there's been too much made about ABI breakage.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我只是觉得大家对 ABI 破坏的讨论太多了。

sentences.en: And I, I, I don't, I don't mean like ABI breakage.
sentences.zh: 我不是指那种 ABI 破坏。

sentences.en: I just mean like, you know, evolved, like, yes, that, that, that's a problem.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，你知道，演进，是的，那确实是个问题。

sentences.en: But I think in a lot of the cases and examples that you have in mind, it's not a question of ABI breakage.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在你脑海中的许多案例和例子里，这根本不是 ABI 破坏的问题。

sentences.en: It's just you're introducing new syntax, new.
sentences.zh: 这只是你引入了新的语法，新的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, but what's the problem?
sentences.zh: 所以，问题到底在哪儿呢？

sentences.en: It doesn't interfere with the old syntax.
sentences.zh: 它并不干扰旧语法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I, I, I don't have, I don't see a problem with that.
sentences.zh: 我没觉得这有什么问题。

sentences.en: And in fact, there have been language proposals for a thing called epics, you know, in this space.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在这个领域已经有关于“史诗”（epics）的语言提案了。

sentences.en: And I, I think at the end of the day, the, the problem is just that the C++ evolution process moves so slowly.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，我认为问题仅仅在于 C++ 的演进过程太慢了。

sentences.en: I think epics, uh, I mean, you can debate about what should go in the new epic.
sentences.zh: 我认为“史诗”，我是说，你可以争论什么应该进入新的“史诗”。

sentences.en: And I think that's really probably where it would slow down.
sentences.zh: 而我认为这可能才是进展缓慢的地方。

sentences.en: Like people think something, what is best?
sentences.zh: 比如人们会想，什么才是最好的？

sentences.en: I don't really believe in codifying like best use or best, you know, best practice.
sentences.zh: 我并不真正相信要编纂什么“最佳用法”或“最佳实践”。

sentences.en: There's another reason why I think you'll get resistance in the committee.
sentences.zh: 我认为你在委员会中会遇到阻力的另一个原因。

sentences.en: I just remembered this, um, there's this fear of creating dialects.
sentences.zh: 我刚想起来，人们害怕创造方言。

sentences.en: There's this fear that if you have like these modes that you opt into, then you create, then
sentences.zh: 人们担心如果你有这些可以选择加入的模式，那么你就会创造出……

sentences.en: C++ becomes sharded into multiple different dialects of C++.
sentences.zh: C++ 就会分裂成多种不同的 C++ 方言。

sentences.en: I, I, I personally think that this is not, uh, uh, not a reasonable argument because we already have dialects.
sentences.zh: 我个人认为这并不是一个合理的论点，因为我们已经有方言了。

sentences.en: You got CUDA.
sentences.zh: 你有 CUDA。

sentences.en: Well, yes, you have CUDA.
sentences.zh: 好吧，是的，你有 CUDA。

sentences.en: Like, you're, you're just one guy who went off and built the C++ compiler.
sentences.zh: 就像你，你只是一个独自去构建 C++ 编译器的人。

sentences.en: And when you want to, you know, when there, when you find a proposal that you find interesting, you can go and rapidly prototype it.
sentences.zh: 当你想要……你知道，当你发现一个你感兴趣的提案时，你可以去快速原型化它。

sentences.en: Um, and I think it's been very refreshing and eyeopening for the C++ world to see that that is possible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为对于 C++ 世界来说，看到这是可能的，是非常令人耳目一新的，也是大开眼界的。

sentences.en: Um, and it, it, not everybody, I think, I, I, certainly, I don't agree with every aspect of your vision of, of the specifics of what you have in mind.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且……并不是每个人，我想，我……当然，我并不完全同意你愿景的每一个方面，关于你脑海中具体细节的那些。

sentences.en: Um, but it seemed like, to me, like, that was sort of besides the point that, that you were showing us a world of possibilities.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但在我看来，那似乎是题外话，你向我们展示了一个充满可能性的世界。

sentences.en: And you don't have to agree with every possibility that Sean showed in that talk.
sentences.zh: 你不必同意 Sean 在那次演讲中展示的每一种可能性。

sentences.en: But that world where we can have all these possibilities, that's very exciting.
sentences.zh: 但那个我们可以拥有所有这些可能性的世界，是非常令人兴奋的。

sentences.en: And then a bunch of people came up and asked questions, nitpicking, like, well, I don't like this and that and that.
sentences.zh: 然后一群人上来问问题，吹毛求疵，说，我不喜欢这个，那个，还有那个。

sentences.en: And it just, it made me so sad because I'm like, but you're missing the point.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到非常难过，因为我想，但你们没抓住重点。

sentences.en: The point is that we have so many options that we can, we can, we can move faster.
sentences.zh: 重点是我们有这么多选择，我们可以……我们可以……我们可以走得更快。

sentences.en: We can explore all of these things.
sentences.zh: 我们可以探索所有这些事情。

sentences.en: We can make the language better.
sentences.zh: 我们可以让语言变得更好。

sentences.en: Um, and people just wanted to focus on it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而人们只想关注那些细节。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think I said something like, um, I'm not trying to convince you of any individual feature.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我说过类似的话，嗯，我不是试图说服你接受任何单一的功能。

sentences.en: I'm just trying to convince you that incremental change will make the language better and more expensive.
sentences.zh: 我只是试图说服你，渐进式的改变会让语言变得更好、更强大。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: But, and what made me sad was that people didn't focus on that.
sentences.zh: 但是，让我难过的是人们没有关注这一点。

sentences.en: Well, I think it's just like, take a beat, you know, like, I, I delivered like 90 minutes of like rapid fire.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得就像是，放轻松，你知道，我……我进行了大约 90 分钟的快速输出。

sentences.en: There's like, I was like, here's like 20 new features, right?
sentences.zh: 就像我当时说，这里有 20 个新功能，对吧？

sentences.en: And, and just like sleep on it at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 至少……至少回去好好想想。

sentences.en: And, and try to look at it from a different angle.
sentences.zh: 试着从不同的角度去看它。

sentences.en: Because I think there's a lot of preconception about what metaprogramming should look like.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为人们对元编程应该是什么样子有很多先入为主的观念。

sentences.en: And my stuff didn't look like that.
sentences.zh: 而我的东西看起来不像那样。

sentences.en: It might have looked more like JavaScript or something else.
sentences.zh: 它可能看起来更像 JavaScript 或其他什么东西。

sentences.en: I mean, I, I didn't really have any individual idiom.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我……我并没有什么特定的惯用法。

sentences.en: I was just trying to do things that would cut, would cut, cut through the nonsense we deal with on a daily basis if you're writing like standard library code.
sentences.zh: 我只是想做一些事情，如果是在写标准库代码，能帮我们解决每天都要面对的那些废话。

sentences.en: Um, and in that sense, it was like very non-ideological.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从这个意义上说，它非常非意识形态化。

sentences.en: I was just trying to get to, you know, complete the problem, you know, finish the problem.
sentences.zh: 我只是想达成……你知道，完成问题，你知道，解决问题。

sentences.en: And I think people just need to like adjust their brains a little bit to, to take, to sit back and say, does this help me solve my problem?
sentences.zh: 我认为人们只需要稍微调整一下大脑，退后一步说，这能帮我解决我的问题吗？

sentences.en: As opposed to, does this conform to some design ideology?
sentences.zh: 而不是，这是否符合某种设计意识形态？

sentences.en: And I think, I think for a long time, C++ has been too much in that Pizani ideology mindset.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，长期以来，C++ 在那种 Pizani 意识形态思维中陷得太深了。

sentences.en: Whereas other languages, they don't have these scruples really.
sentences.zh: 而其他语言，它们真的没有这些顾虑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like if there's something that's super useful, like they'll put it in there, even if it doesn't make any like theoretical sense.
sentences.zh: 比如如果有超级有用的东西，他们就会把它放进去，即使它在理论上没有任何意义。

sentences.en: Uh, and I, you know, going back to the epics, I think the epics thing is a perfect example of that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我，你知道，回到 epics，我认为 epics 就是一个完美的例子。

sentences.en: The, one of the biggest objections to Tunes and Minic epics has been this ideology that you can't have dialects or subsets of C++.
sentences.zh: 对 Tunes 和 Minic epics 最大的反对意见之一就是这种意识形态，即你不能拥有 C++ 的方言或子集。

sentences.en: That it needs to be a, one coherent vision of a language.
sentences.zh: 即它必须是一种语言的单一连贯愿景。

sentences.en: And I, I'm sure that there's a motivation for that, but, um, the, the sort of the absolutism of like that keeping us from doing the,
sentences.zh: 我……我确信这背后有动机，但是，嗯，那种绝对主义……阻止我们去做……

sentences.en: possibly the one thing that could really unlock our future is I think very, uh, very troubling.
sentences.zh: 可能是唯一能真正开启我们未来的事情，我认为非常……非常令人不安。

sentences.en: And, and it's, the way that I've heard that concern expressed has really been sort of this like theoretical, well, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，我听到这种担忧被表达出来的方式，真的只是一种理论上的，嗯，你知道，

sentences.en: we might shard the community in the future if we introduce some notion of, you know, subsets or variants or dialects.
sentences.zh: 如果我们引入某种子集、变体或方言的概念，我们将来可能会分裂社区。

sentences.en: Um, and so we shouldn't, we shouldn't do or encourage that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们不应该……不应该那样做或鼓励那样做。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of things like that where, where we, we, the committee is presented with some option and that option will fix a real problem that we have.
sentences.zh: 有很多这样的事情，委员会被提供了一些选择，而这些选择可以解决我们面临的真正问题。

sentences.en: And, but we don't do that thing because of some theoretical problem that, that might happen if we do that.
sentences.zh: 但是我们没有做那件事，因为如果做了，可能会出现某种理论上的问题。

sentences.en: And it's like, like, you know, the house is on fire.
sentences.zh: 这就像……你知道，房子着火了。

sentences.en: Um, but we don't want to put up the fire because, you know, that could create some other problem.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我们不想灭火，因为，你知道，那可能会制造出其他问题。

sentences.en: Well, maybe we should focus on the problems that we have.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许我们应该专注于我们现有的问题。

sentences.en: There are, I think also we lose sight that there are, you know, like a million full-time C++ programmers.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们还忽略了有……你知道，比如一百万名全职 C++ 程序员。

sentences.en: And it's their livelihood.
sentences.zh: 这是他们的生计。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, if you can make them incrementally more productive, you can make them 5%, 10% more productive.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道，如果你能让他们效率提高一点点，让他们提高 5%、10% 的效率。

sentences.en: That is like industry changing.
sentences.zh: 那将是改变行业的。

sentences.en: That is when you integrate over all of the effort going in, that is, you know, so many billions of dollars of value added.
sentences.zh: 当你整合所有投入的努力时，那就是，你知道，增加了几十亿美元的价值。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I don't think we should like, you know, veto features without really considering the consequence of what we're doing there.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们应该……你知道，在不真正考虑我们所做行为后果的情况下否决功能。

sentences.en: But one of the sad things, and I think you will be intimately familiar with this, um, uh, big tech companies so drastically undervalue developer productivity.
sentences.zh: 但令人难过的事情之一，我想你对此会非常熟悉，嗯……大科技公司严重低估了开发者的生产力。

sentences.en: And, like, this is one of the reasons why there are so few, like, compiler front-end engineers relative to, you know, compiler back-end engineers.
sentences.zh: 而且，这正是为什么相对于编译器后端工程师，编译器前端工程师如此之少的原因之一。

sentences.en: Um, this is why, like, you have so few people working on, um, uh, like, standard libraries and field systems and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是为什么你很少有人在做……嗯……标准库和构建系统之类的事情。

sentences.en: Because, um, at the end of the day, a lot of big tech companies' perspective is like, oh, well, you know, it's painful to write the code.
sentences.zh: 因为，嗯，归根结底，许多大科技公司的观点是，哦，好吧，你知道，写代码很痛苦。

sentences.en: Like, that's okay.
sentences.zh: 那没关系。

sentences.en: Like, we got good developers.
sentences.zh: 我们有优秀的开发者。

sentences.en: Like, they'll, they'll be able to do it.
sentences.zh: 他们……他们能搞定。

sentences.en: And it's like, it's exactly what you said.
sentences.zh: 这就像你刚才说的。

sentences.en: You know, if you make, if you make all your programmers 5% more efficient, that is going to save you so much.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你让所有的程序员效率提高 5%，那将为你节省太多成本。

sentences.en: And, uh, and, and it, it, it is sad that, it is sad the degree to which thing, technologies like compilers are undervalued.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，而且……令人难过的是，令人难过的是编译器这类技术被低估的程度。

sentences.en: Um, uh, you know, especially in this day and age, there used to be a lot more, you know, C++ compiler companies.
sentences.zh: 嗯……你知道，特别是在这个时代，过去有很多……你知道，C++ 编译器公司。

sentences.en: And, um, now there's really only a few and there's only really one front-end company left that's, that's EDG.
sentences.zh: 而现在，真的只有几家了，而且真正剩下的前端公司只有一家，那就是 EDG。

sentences.en: Um, and there's just not the money in the developer tool space that there is in other, um, in other sectors.
sentences.zh: 嗯，开发者工具领域根本没有其他领域那样的资金。

sentences.en: You know, if I, if I go to a programming language conference like C++, like, uh, C++ Now or, uh, C++ Con, back when I went to C++ Con.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我……如果我去参加像 C++ 这样的编程语言会议，比如……C++ Now，或者……C++ Con，我以前去参加 C++ Con 的时候。

sentences.en: Um, um, you go and you see, like, who's sponsoring it and, like, how big, like, the vendor space is.
sentences.zh: 嗯……你去看看，谁在赞助它，以及……供应商空间有多大。

sentences.en: And it's not that large.
sentences.zh: 它并不大。

sentences.en: Um, and then you go to a conference like supercomputing or, like, a conference that, like, sells.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后你去参加像超级计算这样的会议，或者像那种……销售的会议。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's huge, right.
sentences.zh: 是的，规模很大，对吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, where they, where they sell hardware.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们……他们销售硬件的地方。

sentences.en: And it's like, there's so much fun in it.
sentences.zh: 而且那里面有很多乐趣。

sentences.en: The whole exhibition hall is vendors.
sentences.zh: 整个展览大厅都是供应商。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: For switches and things.
sentences.zh: 卖交换机之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, but it's just, we just don't, we don't, we invest in the physical tools that we give to programmers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但只是，我们就是不……我们不投资给程序员提供的物理工具。

sentences.en: We don't invest in the, uh, the, um, the software tools that we give to programmers as much as we should.
sentences.zh: 我们不像我们应该做的那样，投资给程序员提供的软件工具。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But you, but you never answered the question.
sentences.zh: 但你……但你从来没回答那个问题。

sentences.en: What do you think of CPP front?
sentences.zh: 你觉得 CPP front 怎么样？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, so we, I was going to say, we've been talking about, um, carbon and circle and C++.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们……我想说的是，我们一直在谈论……Carbon、Circle 和 C++。

sentences.en: So I guess first question is, did you watch the closing keynote?
sentences.zh: 所以我猜第一个问题是，你看闭幕式主题演讲了吗？

sentences.en: And then second question.
sentences.zh: 然后是第二个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Thoughts on CPP front.
sentences.zh: 对 CPP front 的看法。

sentences.en: And, uh, hopefully the answer to the first one is yes.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，希望第一个问题的答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: And then you can give a little, cause I'm sure that some of our listeners have no idea what we're talking about because they have not seen that keynote yet.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以简单说一下，因为我敢肯定我们的一些听众根本不知道我们在说什么，因为他们还没看过那个主题演讲。

sentences.en: I did not watch the keynote.
sentences.zh: 我没看那个主题演讲。

sentences.en: Wait, wait, Connor, did you watch the keynote?
sentences.zh: 等等，等等，Connor，你看主题演讲了吗？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我参与了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I, uh, I, I was like, I participated in Herb's keynote from the previous year where he showed the pattern matching proposal, which I implemented in circle.
sentences.zh: 我，呃，我当时想，我参加了 Herb 上一年的主题演讲，他在会上展示了模式匹配提案，我已经在 Circle 中实现了它。

sentences.en: And after I sent him that code, he sent me the CPP to doc, which is not public.
sentences.zh: 在我把那段代码发给他之后，他发给了我 CPP2 的文档，那不是公开的。

sentences.en: And that's like 120 pages.
sentences.zh: 那大概有 120 页。

sentences.en: So I read the doc.
sentences.zh: 所以我读了那份文档。

sentences.en: So I have more information than.
sentences.zh: 所以我掌握的信息比（其他人）多。

sentences.en: Wait, so when, this was back at right after last year's CPP gone?
sentences.zh: 等等，所以这是在去年 CppCon 之后吗？

sentences.en: Maybe before, like probably in August of last year.
sentences.zh: 也许更早，大概是去年八月吧。

sentences.en: Interesting, because this is a, uh, what do you call it?
sentences.zh: 有意思，因为这是一个，呃，怎么说呢？

sentences.en: An editorial comment that I had sort of, I thought that this mostly was a reaction.
sentences.zh: 一个编辑评论，我当时觉得这主要是一种回应。

sentences.en: Oh no, this has been, I mean, CPP2 has been around for like a while.
sentences.zh: 哦不，这已经，我是说，CPP2 已经存在一段时间了。

sentences.en: Herb's been working on this for a while.
sentences.zh: Herb 已经研究这个有一阵子了。

sentences.en: I think I first heard of it in.
sentences.zh: 我想我第一次听说它是在……

sentences.en: Herb should have, he should have done this announcement like a couple of years ago.
sentences.zh: Herb 本应该，他本应该在几年前就做这个公告的。

sentences.en: Well, this is, I think, um, I think there's, there's always like this, this, this challenge when you got this new project, like when is it ready to show?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得，呃，我觉得总会有这种挑战，当你有了这个新项目时，什么时候展示它才算准备好了呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's not ready to show, but he said it showed it still.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它还没准备好展示，但他还是展示了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And I think that that's really hard for some people.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这对某些人来说真的很难。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 那没关系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, but I, I think, um, you know, Carbon, I think, picked a good sort of time.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是我觉得，呃，你知道，Carbon，我觉得选了一个不错的时间点。

sentences.en: I mean, one thing that Carbon did was, Carbon didn't, um, you know, go public, you know, like as soon as it was conceived of,
sentences.zh: 我是说，Carbon 做的一件事是，它没有，呃，你知道，在刚构思出来时就公开，

sentences.en: but they had a pretty long period where they brought in more, they brought in more and more.
sentences.zh: 但他们有一段相当长的时间，不断地引入更多的人。

sentences.en: I think Carbon was too early announced.
sentences.zh: 我觉得 Carbon 宣布得太早了。

sentences.en: You think it was too early?
sentences.zh: 你觉得太早了？

sentences.en: Like, yeah, it doesn't, I mean, it doesn't, it didn't even have like not equal operator.
sentences.zh: 对，它甚至连“不等于”运算符都没有。

sentences.en: It didn't have less than, it didn't have integers other than 32 bit.
sentences.zh: 它没有“小于”，除了 32 位之外没有其他整数类型。

sentences.en: It didn't have floats.
sentences.zh: 它没有浮点数。

sentences.en: It didn't, it, it, it, it's not like a, it can't compile anything.
sentences.zh: 它，它，它，它根本不能编译任何东西。

sentences.en: There's no compiler.
sentences.zh: 没有编译器。

sentences.en: I think they should have, they should have got code generation.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们本应该先搞定代码生成。

sentences.en: But I agree that like CPP2, I think would be far more effective and more likely to, to gain traction as an idea if it had been, um, announced earlier.
sentences.zh: 但我同意，如果 CPP2 能早点宣布，作为一种理念，它会更有效，也更有可能获得关注。

sentences.en: I think ditto with things like metaclasses, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 我觉得元类（metaclasses）之类的东西也是一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Cause I, I looked at the repository and it's started in mid 2021 or late 2021.
sentences.zh: 因为我看了代码仓库，它是 2021 年年中或年末开始的。

sentences.en: And, and, and almost all the code contributions happened since July.
sentences.zh: 而且几乎所有的代码贡献都是从七月开始的。

sentences.en: So just like three months ago.
sentences.zh: 所以也就是三个月前。

sentences.en: So, uh, when I was talking to her, he had just started, like, this was last summer.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，当我跟 Herb 谈的时候，他才刚开始，那是去年夏天。

sentences.en: He had just started that repository.
sentences.zh: 他才刚开始那个仓库。

sentences.en: Um, and like he said, it's, it's a, I guess he's calling it a transpiler, but it doesn't like, it's not a compiler.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像他说的，这，我猜他称之为转译器（transpiler），但它并不像，它不是一个编译器。

sentences.en: So, uh, it's a one way, it's a one directional thing, which is not, you can't actually make software that way.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，这是一个单向的东西，你实际上无法用这种方式构建软件。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Like if you're textually, if you call a function, you have to know what the return, the result object type is of that function.
sentences.zh: 比如如果你在文本上调用一个函数，你必须知道该函数的返回结果对象类型是什么。

sentences.en: And there's no way to determine that from, from this architecture he has.
sentences.zh: 而从他目前的架构来看，根本无法确定这一点。

sentences.en: So it's really just a way to show the syntax.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的只是展示语法的一种方式。

sentences.en: I think the, the, the more of the, the real values in that document, which I don't think he's made public still now.
sentences.zh: 我认为那份文档中更有价值的部分，我估计他到现在还没公开。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that is, I guess this is kind of the same, um, I'm not gonna say criticism, but I'm going to say, this is a different philosophy I have from carbon or from CWP2,
sentences.zh: 所以，我想这和对 Carbon 或 CPP2 的看法是一样的，我不会说这是批评，但我会说，这与我对 Carbon 或 CPP2 的理念不同，

sentences.en: which is we can, we can disaggregate these features.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们可以将这些特性解耦。

sentences.en: Like Herb's feature, major feature, I think is the parameter passing.
sentences.zh: 比如 Herb 的主要特性，我认为是参数传递。

sentences.en: He has these, uh, directives like, you know, in, in, out.
sentences.zh: 他有这些指令，比如，in, out。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they may compile to different things.
sentences.zh: 它们可能会编译成不同的东西。

sentences.en: They may emit an R value reference, or it may emit, um, you know, a deep copy or a pass by value.
sentences.zh: 它们可能会生成右值引用，或者生成，呃，深拷贝或按值传递。

sentences.en: If it's like a trivial type, like you can disaggregate that.
sentences.zh: 如果是平凡类型，你可以将其解耦。

sentences.en: And you can say, this is a C++ proposal and we can put that into an existing C++ compiler.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，这是一个 C++ 提案，我们可以把它放入现有的 C++ 编译器中。

sentences.en: And it's just a few, like new bits of syntax.
sentences.zh: 这只是几点新的语法。

sentences.en: And, and I think that's, if you want to show like that, this is a better way to pass parameters that leads to less bugs.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果你想展示这是一种更好的参数传递方式，能减少 Bug，

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 那太好了。

sentences.en: And let's fold it into existing code and we can even rewrite std map or something like that with these, with these, um, new parameter directives.
sentences.zh: 让我们把它整合到现有代码中，我们甚至可以用这些新的参数指令重写 std::map 之类的东西。

sentences.en: I, I kind of wish that he had focused more on the, um, the, the features that, to disaggregate the features of CPV2 and focus on them individually.
sentences.zh: 我有点希望他能更多地关注那些特性，将 CPP2 的特性解耦并单独关注它们。

sentences.en: And he has kind of, like, he does have a proposal for static exceptions.
sentences.zh: 他确实有，比如他有一个静态异常的提案。

sentences.en: And I think there's that, yeah, there is a Metaclass's proposal.
sentences.zh: 而且我想，是的，确实有一个元类提案。

sentences.en: Although these are, again, like five years ago, which is when he started this, this grand vision.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些都是五年前的事了，也就是他开始这个宏大愿景的时候。

sentences.en: I think it's kind of like, um, you know, Rodan, you know, like the whole gates of hell tableau.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有点像，呃，你知道，罗丹的《地狱之门》群雕。

sentences.en: So, but like, people don't want the whole tableau.
sentences.zh: 但人们并不想要整个群雕。

sentences.en: They just want the thinker.
sentences.zh: 他们只想要《思想者》。

sentences.en: So, you know, Herb, just like, give us the thinker.
sentences.zh: 所以，Herb，给我们《思想者》就行了。

sentences.en: And, and the whole tableau is a little bit much to buy into if you care about.
sentences.zh: 如果你在意的话，整个群雕有点让人难以接受。

sentences.en: And just, just in case, uh, our listener is not, um, up to date with this announcement.
sentences.zh: 以防万一，我们的听众还没跟上这个公告。

sentences.en: Basically this CPP front slash CPP two thing is, I don't even really know if it's, you can call it a proposal.
sentences.zh: 基本上这个 CPP/CPP2 的东西，我甚至不知道能不能称之为提案。

sentences.en: Herb in his talk says that's just his sandbox or, you know, for, you know,
sentences.zh: Herb 在演讲中说这只是他的沙盒，或者，你知道，

sentences.en: his sort of dreamland future where he's introducing a whole new syntax and then calling it not a language, but as Sean mentioned,
sentences.zh: 他那种梦幻般的未来，他引入了一套全新的语法，然后称其不是一种语言，但正如 Sean 提到的，

sentences.en: like it transpiles to C++ and it's just a different file extension.
sentences.zh: 它转译成 C++，只是文件扩展名不同。

sentences.en: So you, you know, write this new syntax, call the file dot CPP two, and then it'll generate a dot CPP file, which then ends up getting, getting compiled.
sentences.zh: 所以你写这种新语法，把文件命名为 .cpp2，然后它会生成一个 .cpp 文件，最后被编译。

sentences.en: And there's a bunch of new fancy stuff, the, you know, stuff that just got mentioned, which if you've watched Herb's keynote, I think from the previous year, a couple of years ago,
sentences.zh: 还有一堆新奇的东西，就是刚才提到的那些，如果你看过 Herb 去年的主题演讲，或者几年前的，

sentences.en: he talked about that potentially being something that could show up in C++.
sentences.zh: 他谈到过这可能成为 C++ 中出现的东西。

sentences.en: And, um, yeah, unifies, I think like function and Lambda syntax and there's a bunch of stuff in it.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，是的，统一了函数和 Lambda 语法，里面有很多东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's, I thought the most, I don't know if the most curious thing, but at the beginning of the talk, and it might, might actually be like the most,
sentences.zh: 我觉得最，我不知道是不是最令人好奇的，但在演讲开始时，这可能实际上是，

sentences.en: I don't know what the word is concerning, but I was just like, wow.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该用什么词，令人担忧？但我当时就想，哇。

sentences.en: It made me think of Java from 2018 when I was at Oracle HQ for like a Java 13 party.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起 2018 年我在 Oracle 总部参加 Java 13 派对时的情景。

sentences.en: And one of the people presenting on stage who is like a key Java contributor, I can't remember his name.
sentences.zh: 台上的一位演讲者，他是 Java 的核心贡献者，我不记得他的名字了。

sentences.en: I can find it and put it in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我可以查到并放在节目笔记里。

sentences.en: He went on a big, he got a question from someone in the audience about like some feature in Scala.
sentences.zh: 他当时被观众问到关于 Scala 的某个特性。

sentences.en: And then he went on like a 10 minute monologue of how, you know, Java's not dead.
sentences.zh: 然后他进行了一段 10 分钟的独白，讲 Java 还没死。

sentences.en: And, you know, you can't keep just asking for all these cool features and these functional languages.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你不能一直要求所有这些酷炫的特性和函数式语言的东西。

sentences.en: And I was just like, whoa, man, like it was just a question.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，哇，伙计，那只是个问题而已。

sentences.en: Like, why are you getting so upset just because someone mentioned Scala?
sentences.zh: 为什么有人提到 Scala 你就这么生气？

sentences.en: Because I'm guessing clearly these people that work on Java get a lot of questions.
sentences.zh: 因为我猜这些做 Java 的人肯定经常被问到。

sentences.en: How come we can't have language X, language feature X in Java?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能在 Java 中拥有语言 X 的特性？

sentences.en: And so what Herb said at the beginning, and maybe I'll even, I'll cut the audio clip in, is he basically begs the audience.
sentences.zh: 所以 Herb 在开头说的话，也许我会把音频剪辑放进去，他基本上是在恳求观众。

sentences.en: He says, please don't leave C++.
sentences.zh: 他说，请不要离开 C++。

sentences.en: And I was like, wait, what?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，等等，什么？

sentences.en: But you're at a keynote talk of the, you know, largest, or I guess maybe not by this year's numbers, but, you know, it's sort of known as the, for however many years,
sentences.zh: 但你是在一个主题演讲上，这是最大的，或者我猜也许按今年的数字不是，但你知道，它多年来一直被称为，

sentences.en: the premier North American, I guess it's only one of two, now three.
sentences.zh: 北美首屈一指的会议，我猜现在是三个中的一个。

sentences.en: Anyways, point is, it's a big conference.
sentences.zh: 总之，重点是，这是一个大型会议。

sentences.en: And the closing keynote is like asking the attendees of the conference, like not to leave the language.
sentences.zh: 而闭幕主题演讲竟然是在请求参会者不要离开这门语言。

sentences.en: And I was just kind of shocked that like that, that was being, because like, and like I said, like, as soon as he said that,
sentences.zh: 我当时有点震惊，因为，就像我说的，他一说完，

sentences.en: it made me think of like this meetup that I went to at Oracle HQ where, you know, this guy was basically upset and saying, you know, Java's not dead.
sentences.zh: 就让我想起我在 Oracle 总部参加的那个聚会，那个人基本上很生气，说 Java 没死。

sentences.en: We got millions of people, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 我们有数百万用户，等等等等。

sentences.en: And I was like, well, I mean, the second you start saying something's not, like, it's like, you know, when they say, oh, smart people don't say they're smart.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，嗯，当你开始说某样东西没死时，就像人们说“聪明人不会说自己聪明”一样。

sentences.en: You know, it's like, it's one of those things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: It's anyways, it was, so like I said, I'm not sure if the word is concerning, but I just, I, I thought it was odd to, um, and that made me even think is like,
sentences.zh: 总之，就像我说的，我不确定“担忧”这个词是否准确，但我只是觉得这很奇怪，而且这让我甚至在想，

sentences.en: is this like actually like some inflection point?
sentences.zh: 这是否真的是某种转折点？

sentences.en: And is it the beginning of the end?
sentences.zh: 这是终结的开始吗？

sentences.en: We're seeing all these suggestions.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了所有这些建议。

sentences.en: I think it's definitely an inflection point.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是一个转折点。

sentences.en: I think whether it's the beginning of the end is, is a question up to, um, our user base and also the, the leadership.
sentences.zh: 至于这是否是终结的开始，取决于我们的用户群以及领导层。

sentences.en: Like, what, what, what, what do you think, Sean?
sentences.zh: 那么，Sean，你怎么看？

sentences.en: Like what, if you could, what do you think of that?
sentences.zh: 如果你能说的话，你对此怎么看？

sentences.en: And like, also like, if you had a crystal ball or you had to bet, you know, five, 10 years from now, what do you, what do you think the low level language space is going to,
sentences.zh: 还有，如果你有一个水晶球，或者必须打赌，五年、十年后，你认为底层语言领域会变成什么样？

sentences.en: is everyone going to be writing in circle?
sentences.zh: 大家都会用 Circle 编写吗？

sentences.en: Is it going to be C++ is just going to be in slow decline or?
sentences.zh: 还是 C++ 会缓慢衰落？

sentences.en: Tune in next time to hear Sean's answer and part two of this episode.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听下期节目，听听 Sean 的回答和本集的下半部分。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoyed and have a great day.
sentences.zh: 希望你喜欢，祝你有愉快的一天。
